description: The default retry mode is now `standard`, and the `standard` and `adaptive` (`RetryMode.ADAPTIVE_V2`) retry modes now use retry behavior 2.1 for clients that use a retry strategy, which is the default. The `AWS_NEW_RETRIES_2026` environment variable and `aws.newRetries2026` system property are now ignored, and the SDK logs a warning when either is set to a value other than `true`. Retry behavior 2.1 uses a 50 ms base backoff (1 s for throttling errors), a retry quota cost of 14 tokens per retry (5 for throttling errors), and 3 attempts by default. DynamoDB clients default to 4 attempts with a 25 ms base backoff, but use the generic defaults when a retry mode or retry strategy configurator is set on the client or in a plugin. Because each retry costs more of the 500-token quota, many concurrent failures exhaust it sooner, for example in large S3 multipart downloads. Retry behavior 2.1 also treats `LimitExceededException` as a retryable throttling error, honors the `max_attempts` property of the client's profile (the public static retry strategy factories, such as `AwsRetryStrategy.standardRetryStrategy()`, read the active profile in the default profile files), takes the server-suggested delay from the `x-amz-retry-after` header instead of `Retry-After` (clamped to at most 5 s more than the computed backoff), and backs off before failing long-polling operations when the retry quota is exhausted. A `RetryPolicy` built without a retry mode, including `AwsRetryPolicy.defaultRetryPolicy()`, now uses the `standard` retry mode with its previous `standard` behavior instead of `legacy`. Kinesis clients now use a retry strategy instead of a Kinesis-specific `RetryPolicy`, and retry `SubscribeToShard` like other operations in every retry mode. To turn this off, use a separate client configured with `retryStrategy(r -> r.maxAttempts(1))`, or add a request plugin that sets it on `SubscribeToShardRequest`. Apart from Kinesis, the `legacy` retry mode and the deprecated `RetryMode.ADAPTIVE` are unchanged. A DynamoDB module older than this release, used with this version of the core modules, keeps its retry behavior 2.0 settings, so it defaults to the `standard` retry mode with 9 attempts. An STS module older than this release uses the generic retry behavior 2.1 strategy in the `standard` and `adaptive` retry modes, without retrying `IDPCommunicationError`; upgrade the STS module to get that retry. A Kinesis module older than this release keeps its Kinesis-specific `RetryPolicy`, which now defaults to the `standard` retry mode without retry behavior 2.1, and still doesn't retry `SubscribeToShard`. To keep the previous default behavior, set the retry mode to `legacy`, for example with `AWS_RETRY_MODE=legacy`, `-Daws.retryMode=legacy`, or `retry_mode = legacy` in your profile.
